formation.title: The Birth of Prussia
formation.text:
The transformation is complete. From the ashes of the Teutonic Order and the sandy marches of Brandenburg, a new state has emerged: Prussia. We have broken the power of the clergy, bound the Junker nobility to our service, and imposed order upon a fractured land. Now the question stands before us: what kind of kingdom shall we build?

Will we follow the path of iron, drilling our soldiers into the finest army in Europe, making war our industry and discipline our creed? Or shall we seek to become a beacon of enlightened governance, investing in schools, reforming our laws, and building a state that earns the admiration of philosophers as much as the fear of generals?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: The Iron Kingdom
modifiers.text: Prussia is not a state that possesses an army: it is an army that possesses a state. The Hohenzollern kingdom has forged itself into the most militarized society in Europe, where discipline, obedience, and martial virtue form the bedrock of national identity.

options.text: A kingdom of reason and law.

modifiers.name: The Enlightened State
modifiers.text: From the Pietist schools of Halle to the legal reforms of Frederick, Prussia has pursued a vision of rational governance. An efficient bureaucracy, universal education, and codified law transform a poor northern march into an engine of progress.

advances.name: Teutonic Heritage
advances.text: The martial traditions and fortress-building legacy of the Teutonic Order laid the foundations for Prussia's military culture.

advances.name: Baltic Amber Trade
advances.text: Since the Teutonic Knights seized control of Konigsberg, the amber trade has been a Prussian monopoly. The golden stone of the Baltic fuels commerce and artisanship.

advances.name: Grain of the Vistula
advances.text: The rye and wheat of Prussia, Mazovia and Lithuania come down the Vistula and the Pregel on rafts and barges to the Prussian ports, where the Order's own grand stewards and the town merchants ship them on to Flanders and England.

advances.name: Courts of Arthur
advances.text: Thorn, Elbing, Danzig, Kulm, Braunsberg and Konigsberg: the great towns of Prussia are ruled by merchant families who trade with the Hansa and meet in halls named for King Arthur's court.

advances.name: Junker Estates
advances.text: The Junker landed aristocracy forms the backbone of the Prussian state. Their vast Ritterguter estates supply both the tax base and the officer corps that make Prussia formidable.

advances.name: Ordensburg Tradition
advances.text: The massive brick fortresses of the Teutonic Order (Marienburg, Konigsberg, Balga) established a tradition of military architecture that shaped Prussian defensive doctrine for centuries.

advances.name: The Prussian Confederation
advances.text: In 1440 the towns and the gentry of Prussia swore a league at Marienwerder against arbitrary rule. When it came to war the towns paid for it: Danzig's credit bought the fortress of Marienburg from the garrison's own unpaid companies. No ruler of Prussia has since governed without the estates.

advances.name: The Coinage Reform
advances.text: Nicolaus Copernicus, canon of Frauenburg, laid his treatise on money before the Prussian diet at Graudenz in 1522: debased coin drives good coin out of the land and ruins it. The Prussian coinage was called in and struck anew on his lines in 1528.

advances.name: Prussian Arms Manufacture
advances.text: Prussian iron foundries and weapons workshops supply the growing army with standardized, reliable armaments.

advances.name: Ducal Consolidation
advances.text: The transformation of the Duchy of Prussia from a Polish fief into a sovereign state required steady administrative consolidation and the assertion of ducal authority over fractious local interests.

advances.name: Totenkopf Hussar Tradition
advances.text: Frederick the Great transformed the hussars from ornamental cavalry into a decisive arm of war. The Totenkopf Hussars, wearing the death's head on their mirlitons, became the most feared light cavalry in Europe.

advances.name: Cameralism
advances.text: The Prussian science of state finance, Cameralism, treated the kingdom as a great estate to be managed with efficiency and foresight, centralizing revenue collection through Domänenkammern.

advances.name: Prussian Officer Corps
advances.text: The Cadettenhaus system trains Junker sons from childhood in military science, creating a professional officer corps bound by duty, honor, and absolute loyalty to the crown.

advances.name: Cantonment System
advances.text: The Kantonreglement of 1733 divided Prussia into recruitment cantons, making every male subject a potential soldier. This gave Prussia an army vastly disproportionate to its population.

event.title: The Cantonment System
event.text:
In 1733, King Frederick William I issued the Kantonreglement, dividing the kingdom into recruitment districts, cantons, each assigned to a regiment. Every able-bodied male is enrolled from birth, serving in peacetime through rotating furloughs and returning to their fields between training periods. The Junker officers command peasants from their own estates, creating bonds of loyalty that run deeper than mere military discipline.

This system gives Prussia an army far larger than its population should support: 3.6% of the total population under arms, the highest proportion in Europe. The question is how we apply this extraordinary resource.

options.text: Drill them relentlessly. Quality over quantity.

modifiers.name: Cantonment Drill
modifiers.text: Relentless drill and discipline transform raw Kantonist recruits into soldiers of exceptional quality.

options.text: Maximize efficiency. Every Kantonist serves twice: as soldier and as farmer.

modifiers.name: Cantonment Efficiency
modifiers.text: The cantonment system maximizes every resource: soldiers return to their farms between campaigns, feeding the kingdom while standing ready to march.

advances.name: Oblique Order Tactics
advances.text: Frederick the Great's perfection of the oblique order, massing force against the enemy's weakest point while refusing the opposite flank, revolutionized European warfare at Leuthen and Rossbach.

event.title: The Oblique Order of Battle
event.text:
At Leuthen in December 1757, Frederick demonstrated the devastating potential of the oblique order: concentrating overwhelming force against the weakest point of the enemy line while refusing the opposite flank. With 36,000 Prussians against 66,000 Austrians, the king executed a perfect march across the enemy front, struck their exposed left flank, and rolled up the entire Austrian army in one of the most decisive victories in military history.

Coming just weeks after the equally stunning victory at Rossbach, Leuthen established Prussian tactical doctrine as the standard against which all European armies would measure themselves. Shall we press this advantage offensively, or use these principles to perfect our defensive warfare?

options.text: Strike where they are weakest. The oblique attack is our sword.

modifiers.name: The Oblique Attack
modifiers.text: Concentrate force at the decisive point. Strike where the enemy is weakest and shatter their line before they can react.

options.text: Hold where we are strongest. Let the enemy break upon our lines.

modifiers.name: The Oblique Defense
modifiers.text: Refuse the weaker flank and present an impenetrable front. Let the enemy exhaust themselves against disciplined firepower.

advances.name: The General Staff
advances.text: The Grosser Generalstab, born from the ashes of the 1806 defeat, was the world's first permanent military planning body. Officers selected by merit and trained in strategic thinking at the Kriegsakademie.

event.title: The Grosser Generalstab
event.text:
Following the catastrophe of Jena-Auerstedt in 1806, reformers led by Gerhard von Scharnhorst and August von Gneisenau rebuilt the Prussian military from its foundations. In 1810, the Kriegsakademie opened its doors, selecting officers by demonstrated intelligence and merit rather than birth alone. The Great General Staff, the Grosser Generalstab, became the first permanent military planning body in history, responsible for the continuous study of war in all its dimensions.

Its officers are trained to think independently, to make decisions in the absence of orders, and to coordinate operations across vast distances. This institution will shape the practice of warfare for the next century and beyond.

options.text: An army that thinks as one mind.

advances.name: Feldjaeger Corps
advances.text: The Reitende Feldjaeger, mounted scouts and riflemen, served as the eyes and couriers of the Prussian General Staff, combining mobility with marksmanship.

advances.name: Allgemeines Landrecht
advances.text: The General State Laws of 1794 unified Prussian jurisprudence under a single rational code: an absolute monarchy binding itself to the rule of law.

event.title: The Allgemeines Landrecht
event.text:
In 1794, Prussia promulgated the Allgemeines Landrecht fur die Preussischen Staaten, the General State Laws, a comprehensive legal code that sought to unify the diverse provincial legal systems of the kingdom under a single framework. Drafted under the orders of Frederick the Great and completed by Carl Gottlieb Svarez, the code represents a remarkable achievement: an absolute monarchy voluntarily binding itself to the rule of law.

The Landrecht guaranteed prompt and impartial administration of justice, protected subjects against arbitrary royal will, and established legal protections for property and contract. It was not democratic, it preserved estate-based social distinctions, but it was rational, predictable, and fair within its own terms.

options.text: The law above all: even the king.

destiny.name: The Prussian Destiny
destiny.text: Prussia has been forged. Now it must find its place among the great powers of Europe. Maintain stability as we chart our course.

event.title: The Prussian Destiny
event.text:
The Prussian state stands at a crossroads. Behind us lie the marshes of Brandenburg and the ruined castles of the Teutonic Order. Before us stretches the future of a nation that has already defied the odds merely by existing. A kingdom built on sand, surrounded by enemies on every side, with no natural frontiers and few resources beyond the discipline of its people.

Yet it is precisely this adversity that has forged the Prussian character. We cannot afford the luxury of complacency. Every generation must earn anew what the last has built. The question is not whether Prussia will act, but in which direction we shall march.

destiny.name: The Silesian Conquest
destiny.text: Seize the wealthy province of Silesia from the Habsburgs. Control of Wroclaw and its industries will transform Prussia from a minor kingdom into a true military power. Requires 30,000 men under arms.

event.title: The Rape of Silesia
event.text:
When the young king mounted the throne and learned that the Habsburg emperor had died leaving only a daughter to inherit, he saw an opportunity that history offers perhaps once in a century. Without declaration of war, without diplomatic pretext, Prussian columns marched into Silesia, one of the richest provinces in Central Europe, with its linen manufactories, iron mines, and teeming population.

The seizure was a calculated gamble of the highest order. Every great power in Europe would oppose us. But Silesia doubles our population, triples our industry, and transforms Prussia from a curiosity into a contender. The conquest is complete. Now we must hold it.

destiny.name: The Frederician Wars
destiny.text: Expand Prussian dominion over Saxony and Pomerania. The conquest of Dresden and Stettin will secure our flanks and demonstrate that Prussia can hold what it seizes against all of Europe. Requires 2,000 gold in the treasury.

event.title: The Seven Years' War
event.text:
Prussia has survived the nightmare. Encircled by France, Austria, Russia, Sweden, and Saxony simultaneously (outnumbered five to one in every theater), the kingdom fought for seven years on the edge of annihilation. At Rossbach, at Leuthen, at Zorndorf, Prussian arms prevailed through speed, discipline, and the sheer refusal to accept defeat.

The war has devastated our lands but proven our mettle. Every court in Europe now treats Prussia as a great power. How shall we capitalize on this survival?

options.text: Press our advantage. Seize the initiative.

modifiers.name: Rapid Conquest Doctrine
modifiers.text: Strike before the enemy can prepare. Swift wars of aggression seize territory faster than coalitions can form against us, at the cost of diplomatic standing.

options.text: Consolidate and fortify what we hold.

modifiers.name: Iron Consolidation
modifiers.text: Fortify every conquest, suppress every rebellion, and field an army that no alliance dares challenge.

destiny.name: The Soldier King's Legacy
destiny.text: Complete the domination of northern Germany. Berlin, Magdeburg, and Hanover must fall under Prussian control. It is the work of the Soldier King's age, when the canton system of 1733 let a poor kingdom keep a great army. With 75,000 soldiers and unrivaled prestige, Prussia will stand as the paramount military power of the continent.

event.title: Master of Northern Germany
event.text:
The work of generations is complete. From Konigsberg to the Rhine, from the Baltic to the Harz Mountains, Prussian authority extends across the breadth of northern Germany. Berlin has grown from a provincial garrison town into one of Europe's great capitals. Magdeburg, the strongest fortress on the Elbe, guards our heartland. Hanover, once the seat of a rival electorate, now answers to our crown.

Prussia commands the largest and finest army on the continent. The question before us now is how we shall wield this unprecedented power.

options.text: Total mobilization. Every resource serves the army.

modifiers.name: Total Mobilization
modifiers.text: Every resource in the kingdom serves the war machine. Raw materials flow to foundries and arsenals, and the population accepts the burdens of military supremacy, even at the cost of court expenditures.

modifiers.name: Prussian Hegemony
modifiers.text: The crowned eagle of Prussia commands universal respect. Legitimate authority, cultural influence, and satisfied estates make the kingdom the arbiter of Central European affairs.

destiny.name: The Pietist Schools
destiny.text: August Hermann Francke's educational revolution at Halle showed what rational governance could achieve. Seize Halle and found a Library there, as Francke's foundations kept one beside their orphanage and schools, to lay the foundations of an enlightened state.

conditions.text: We own Halle and it has a Library

event.title: The Francke Foundations
event.text:
In the university town of Halle, the Pietist theologian August Hermann Francke has built something unprecedented: an entire educational complex encompassing an orphanage, schools for the poor, a pharmacy, a printing press, and a teachers' seminary. The Franckesche Stiftungen demonstrate that systematic investment in human capital yields returns no mere treasury can match.

Francke's methods (practical education, universal literacy, rational curriculum) have attracted attention across Europe. They represent the seed of something larger: a state that derives its strength not from soldiers but from the quality of its citizens.

options.text: Reason is the foundation of the state.

destiny.name: The Cameralist Model
destiny.text: Build a state that runs like a well-oiled machine. The plague of 1709 emptied Prussian Lithuania; Frederick William I resettled it from Gumbinnen with Salzburg exiles and set a War and Domains Chamber over it. Hold Gumbinnen and raise it to 20 development, amass 2,000 gold, and ensure books are traded in the capital market to fuel the Prussian bureaucracy.

conditions.text: We own Gumbinnen and its development is at least 20

children.text: Books is produced in the market
Books is traded in the market

event.title: The Cameralist Revolution
event.text:
The Prussian model of governance has matured into a science. The Cameralists (state economists trained at Halle and Frankfurt an der Oder) treat the kingdom as a single vast estate to be managed with precision. Every forest, mine, manufactory, and customs house is inventoried, taxed, and optimized.

The result is a state of remarkable efficiency. Prussia collects more revenue per capita than France, builds more roads per square mile than England, and educates more children per parish than any kingdom in Europe. Two schools of thought compete for influence.

options.text: The state must build. Invest in infrastructure.

modifiers.name: Mercantilist Efficiency
modifiers.text: The Cameralist state directs investment into infrastructure and industry, reducing building costs, boosting production, and empowering Prussian merchants.

options.text: Knowledge is wealth. Invest in minds.

modifiers.name: Wissensgesellschaft
modifiers.text: A society organized around knowledge. Prussian universities, spy networks, and diplomatic channels spread influence and gather intelligence with unmatched effectiveness.

destiny.name: The Aufklarung
destiny.text: Make Prussia the intellectual capital of Europe. Seize Leipzig (the publishing heart of the continent), hold Konigsberg, the city of the Albertina and of Kant, and raise it to 43 development, achieve the highest prestige, and seat a Supreme Court in the capital, as Frederick II reformed the courts and ordered the General Code of the Prussian states.

conditions.text: We own Konigsberg and its development is at least 43

event.title: The Aufklarung Triumphant
event.text:
Leipzig, the publishing capital of Europe, now operates under Prussian law. Its book fairs distribute the ideas of Kant, Lessing, and Moses Mendelssohn across the continent. Prussian universities lead the world in philosophy, theology, and the natural sciences. The Allgemeines Landrecht has codified the most comprehensive legal system in Europe.

Frederick's vision of an enlightened state has been realized beyond anything he could have imagined. Prussia is admired not for the size of its army but for the quality of its governance, the tolerance of its society, and the brilliance of its thinkers. Two visions of enlightened governance now compete for the future.

modifiers.name: Enlightened Absolutism
modifiers.text: The philosopher-king rules for all his subjects equally. Religious tolerance, cultural integration, and acceptance of diversity strengthen the state from within.

modifiers.name: Verfassungsstaat
modifiers.text: A constitutional state governed by law, not royal whim. Population growth flourishes under stable institutions, while fiscal reform reduces the cost of both war and debt.

units.name: Totenkopf Hussars
units.text: Elite shock cavalry wearing the death's head insignia. Fast, aggressive, and utterly fearless: the terror of enemy flanks and supply lines.

units.name: Feldjaeger
units.text: Light riflemen trained as scouts and skirmishers. Expert marksmen who screen the army's advance and harass enemy formations before the main assault.

units.name: Kantonist
units.text: Conscript soldiers raised through the cantonment system. Peasants trained from youth, they serve their regiment in war and their Junker's fields in peace.

buildings.name: Cadettenhaus
buildings.text: A Prussian military academy training the sons of the Junker nobility in tactics, drill, and the science of war from an early age.

buildings.name: Domanenkammer
buildings.text: A Cameralist revenue office that administers crown lands and centralizes tax collection with Prussian efficiency.

buildings.name: Amber Guild
buildings.text: A guild hall where master craftsmen process raw Baltic amber into luxury goods, jewelry, and decorative pieces: a tradition dating to the Teutonic Order's monopoly over Konigsberg.

buildings.name: Quay Granary
buildings.text: A tall brick Speicher on the waterfront. Grain that came down the river on rafts and barges is measured, stored and turned here until a sea ship takes it west. Danzig filled a whole island with such granaries.

buildings.name: Court of Arthur
buildings.text: The Artushof, the hall of a Prussian town's merchant brotherhoods. Each brotherhood has its bench; here ships are chartered, quarrels settled, envoys feasted, and the town's mind made up before the council meets.

buildings.name: Rittergut
buildings.text: A knightly estate farmed for the grain trade. The lord works his own fields with the labor of peasants bound to the soil, and sends the harvest downriver. The estate yields more grain, and the district answers to its Junker.

children.text: The location's raw material is Wheat
The location's raw material is Sturdy Grains

buildings.name: Arms Foundry
buildings.text: A Prussian weapons workshop producing standardized muskets, bayonets, and ammunition for the growing army.

buildings.name: Kriegsakademie
buildings.text: The Prussian War College, successor to Scharnhorst's Kriegsakademie, trains officers in the art of command through rigorous study of strategy, tactics, and military history.

buildings.name: Universitat
buildings.text: A Prussian research university in the Humboldtian tradition, uniting teaching and research. Its faculties advance knowledge in philosophy, natural science, and law.

list.name: Generaldirektorium
list.text: The General Superior Directory of Finance, War, and Domains, established by Frederick William I on 20 December 1722 and effective from 1723. It merged the rival General Finance Directory and General War Commissariat into a single collegial body presided over by the king himself, with five vice-presidents and fourteen councillors selected for expertise rather than birth. Its provincial Kriegs- und Domaenenkammern bypassed the noble Staende of the Junkertum and tied financial, military, and domanial administration directly to the throne. In East Prussia the land tax they gathered fell on noble estates as on peasant farms. The Directory doubled crown revenue between 1715 and 1740 and produced the absolutist apparatus that underpinned every later Hohenzollern campaign.

list.name: Kantonsystem
list.text: The cantonal recruitment regulation of 1733, by which Frederick William I divided the realm into geographically defined Kantone each tied to a specific infantry regiment. Robust peasant sons were enrolled at adolescence and called up for two months of training each spring, returning to the fields outside campaign season; the system thus sustained the proportionally largest army in Europe without crippling the agrarian base. Nobles, urban burghers, only sons of farmers, foreigners, and craftsmen of value were unconditionally exempt. The burden of conscription fell on the peasantry of the eastern provinces, binding them ever more tightly to their lords' estates.

list.name: Generaladjutantur
list.text: The office of the king's adjutants general, through which every commission, promotion and leave in the Prussian army passes. Under Frederick William I it keeps the rank list of each regiment and a yearly conduct list on every officer, and the king reads them himself. Commissions are kept for the nobility: after 1763 Frederick II removes most of the commoners who were made officers during the war. Out of this office the Military Cabinet of the reform years grows.

list.name: Allgemeines Landrecht
list.text: The General State Laws for the Prussian States, drafted under Frederick II by Carl Gottlieb Svarez and Ernst Ferdinand Klein and promulgated on 5 February 1794. Across some seventeen thousand articles it imposed a uniform rational law on every Prussian province, codifying civil, penal, family, and administrative law in a single compendium and binding even the king to its provisions: a striking concession by absolute monarchy to the rule of law. Its preservation of the Staendegesellschaft and of east-Elbian serfdom reflected its transitional character; nonetheless the Landrecht governed Prussia until the Imperial Civil Code of 1900.

list.name: Domaenenkammern
list.text: The provincial Kriegs- und Domaenenkammern, presided over by a chamber-president and staffed by salaried councillors trained in the cameralist sciences. They administered the royal demesne, leased crown lands on short productivity-based contracts, and supervised tax collection in the towns through subordinate Steuerraete. By substituting professional fiscal expertise for the bargaining of the noble Landstaende, the Chambers extracted revenue with a discipline unmatched in Europe; the salaried civil servant of nineteenth-century continental tradition is their direct descendant.

list.name: Grosser Generalstab
list.text: The Great General Staff, organized after the catastrophe of Jena-Auerstedt in 1806 by Scharnhorst, Gneisenau, and the Military Reorganization Commission, and formalized in law in 1814. Its officers continuously studied mobilization plans, prepared the operational maps of every probable theatre, and drilled the doctrine of Auftragstaktik in which a subordinate executes the commander's intent rather than awaiting explicit orders. Promotion was by competitive examination and demonstrated competence rather than by birth: a rebuke to the Junker officer corps that ran in parallel with it for the rest of the century, and a model that every modern army would eventually copy.

list.name: Kriegsakademie
list.text: The Allgemeine Kriegsschule, founded in Berlin by Gerhard von Scharnhorst on 15 October 1810 as one of three colleges intended to produce a professional staff officer cadre. Three years of mathematics, physics, military history, applied tactics, and staff rides were prerequisite for appointment to the Grosser Generalstab. Carl von Clausewitz had studied at its predecessor institution under Scharnhorst himself; Helmuth von Moltke the Elder taught there in the 1820s. The Akademie's graduates (drawn substantially from non-noble backgrounds) formed the intellectual core of the Prussian and later German army.
